aggregation.en: Percentile P95 (linear interpolation, Hyndman-Fan type 7) of daily precipitation on wet days (>= 1 mm) of 1991–2020. Computed only when every day of the baseline is valid.

limitations.en: Regional signal: value of the grid cell that contains the site point (about 50-100 km), not a field measurement; no downscaling (ADR-3).
Daily values follow the time standard reported by the API (LST).
ETCCDI uses the 1961–1990 base period; POWER starts in 1981, so the baseline here is 1991–2020 (ADR-3).
Grid-cell precipitation smooths local storms: the percentile is lower than at a rain gauge.

Ground check (team analysis, Cruz Alta, RS, Brazil; INMET station A853 and ANA rain gauge 2853015): POWER flags rain (1 mm or more) on 38-41% of days against 24-28% at the gauges, so dry spells are shorter in POWER (longest January-February dry spell 7.3 days on average against 11.7 at gauge 2853015, 41 seasons) and heavy rain is smoothed (on days with 60 mm or more at the gauge, POWER recorded 46-57% of the amount; a neighbouring gauge, 66-68%). Dry spells and extreme rain from POWER underestimate what a rain gauge records: check them against a rain gauge or GPM IMERG (daily r with A853: 0.85 for IMERG, 0.78 for POWER). Monthly totals agree better (monthly r with A853: 0.92). Details: Data & Methods, #satellite-vs-ground-check.

limitations.en: Modeled (reanalysis-based) data, labeled 'modeled' (FR9).
Regional signal: value of the grid cell that contains the site point (about 50-100 km), not a field measurement; no downscaling (ADR-3).
Daily values follow the time standard reported by the API (LST).

Ground check (team analysis, Cruz Alta, RS, Brazil; INMET station A853 and ANA rain gauge 2853015): POWER flags rain (1 mm or more) on 38-41% of days against 24-28% at the gauges, so dry spells are shorter in POWER (longest January-February dry spell 7.3 days on average against 11.7 at gauge 2853015, 41 seasons) and heavy rain is smoothed (on days with 60 mm or more at the gauge, POWER recorded 46-57% of the amount; a neighbouring gauge, 66-68%). Dry spells and extreme rain from POWER underestimate what a rain gauge records: check them against a rain gauge or GPM IMERG (daily r with A853: 0.85 for IMERG, 0.78 for POWER). Monthly totals agree better (monthly r with A853: 0.92). Details: Data & Methods, #satellite-vs-ground-check.
